variant_perception_summary: Nu's operating growth is known and the sell side remains constructive. The provisional difference is that current spread and revenue gains arrive before the full credit-loss outcome and H1 net income included a large deferred-tax benefit, while the current price sits above every engine fair-value case. The edge is not proven because the group cost of equity is unresolved.
what_everyone_knows: Nu is a fast-growing Latin American digital bank with 139 million Q2 customers, 83.5% activity and strong Q2 revenue/EPS growth.
what_is_priced_in: US$14.30 and a US$18.78 mean sell-side target price reflect continued high growth and returns; at a 16.51% cost of equity the current price requires 47.36% terminal ROE or 80.89% FY2027–30 profit growth, while 9.78% reconciles the same path.
what_market_may_be_missing: Current credit-income and lower-credit-cost benefits may precede later losses, and the US$991.046m H1 deferred-tax benefit makes the period less cash-backed than headline net income suggests; neither point proves improper accounting.
edge_proof: The edge is proven only if a sourced group-wide cost of equity is materially above 9.78% and the Q3 filing misses the raised revenue/EPS bar or shows worse credit quality; it is falsified by a defensible group rate at or below 9.78% and a material Q3 dual beat with stable or better credit metrics.
killer_risk: The modeled group discount rate is wrong: 16.51% is a Brazil Investments CGU rate, while 9.78% reconciles the same earnings path to the market price.

red_flags.description: Five High findings converge on one credit-cycle risk: spread durability, the raised FQ3 bar, lender-specific cash/accrual divergence, the US$991.046m deferred-tax benefit and the US$504.700m downside-macro allowance bound. These are not proof of a misstatement.
KPMG Brazil was censured and fined US$700,000 by the PCAOB for work involving another issuer; Nu was not named. Nu's FY2023–FY2025 audit opinions were clean and FY2025 ICFR was effective.

Recurring share-based compensation is excluded from adjusted net income; the FY2025 US$359.0m addback produced a US$203.7m after-tax or 7.1% uplift. This is a candor concern, not evidence of misstatement.
